chapter: Duke, Eddie Lang and other guitarists
title: Guitarists in New York: Eddie Lang compared
summary: There were few single-string guitarists in New York; he heard Eddie Lang with Crosby and Whiteman and says Lang lacked ideas.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: At the time you played with Duke there weren't too many guitarists around New York, were there? Playing at the level --
Because I was just thinking, where else -- in New York. In Philly there were a couple of players.
Like Lonny Johnson, Bobby Leecan and so forth.
Yeah. Did you know Bobby Leecan?
No. I just heard one of his recordings. Just recently heard one of his recordings.
Way back, too. There wasn't anybody else in New York, though, that you can remember?
Did you ever hear Eddie Lang play --
-- in those days? Ever heard him play? Who with, Bing Crosby, or --
And Whiteman, Paul Whiteman. That's the first time I heard him, with Crosby, Eddie Lang -- what's his name?
Yeah, but I'm talking about the one you were talking about.
Yeah. What did you think of his playing, what you remember?
He wasn't up to the point, though.
See, he was single string and I was single string.
He wasn't up to the point but he come home on time.
By the point I mean that he didn't have no founding.
No founding. And not come back to the melody. That's what I saw. Now, I don't know about anybody else seeing it.
The type I played, I mean it was a lot different. Because I can hear it. A lot of these guitar
players is coming up here lately. You can hear the same thing. They don't have the ideas. If they have it they never use it.
Because they're supposed to have it if they understand what they are doing.
Uh-huh. Well, you feel like -- in other words, if I understand, there's more people now with the technique that can get around the instrument, that know the instrument.
But that doesn't mean that there's as many people -- there's still no more people with ideas.
Just a lot more people that can play.
There ain't nobody got the ideas about trying to make them some good money, you know what I mean?
It's slowed down. It's slowed down. Any guitar player can get up with a guitar and play. (Singing). He's making pretty good money.
